title: The primer sequences of targeted genes.
author: Arghavan Zebardast
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0

steps.title: Collect oropharyngeal swabs
steps.instruction: Obtain oropharyngeal swab samples from participants (with written informed consent) and store them under conditions suitable for viral nucleic‑acid preservation.

steps.title: Extract viral nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Perform genome extraction from each swab sample using a viral RNA extraction kit, following the kit’s recommended protocol.

steps.title: Amplify target genes by RT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Run conventional multiplex RT‑PCR assays with the primer sequences of the targeted genes (SARS‑CoV‑2, Influenza A H1N1/H3N2, Influenza B, RSV, adenovirus, enterovirus, parainfluenza) on the extracted nucleic acids.

steps.title: Prepare barcoded sequencing libraries
steps.instruction: Convert the RT‑PCR products into sequencing libraries, attach a unique barcode to each sample, and pool the barcoded libraries according to the Oxford Nanopore library‑preparation workflow.

steps.title: Run MinION sequencing
steps.instruction: Load the pooled barcoded library onto a MinION flow cell and perform a 12‑hour sequencing run.

substeps.instruction: Load flow cell onto the MinION device.
Start the sequencing run and monitor for 12 hours.

steps.title: Quality‑filter raw reads
steps.instruction: After sequencing, filter the raw reads to retain only those with a Q‑score greater than 7; in this study 711,000 reads passed the quality filter.

steps.title: Analyze data for virus detection
steps.instruction: Use bioinformatic tools to map quality‑filtered reads to the 12 target viral genes, require a Q30 value greater than 1 % and more than 90 % genome coverage for a positive call; eleven of the twelve target genes were identified with >90 % coverage.

steps.title: Assess assay performance
steps.instruction: Determine sensitivity by testing serial dilutions of samples and different primer pools; measure detection limits for SARS‑CoV‑2, Influenza A (H1N1, H3N2), Influenza B, and RSV. Calculate specificity (99.9 %) using 20 known‑positive clinical samples.
